title: Why the Eiffel Tower grows every summer
angle: A 7,300-tonne iron tower that changes height with the weather — how?
through_line: the tower's silhouette, measured against a ruler

blocks.line: Every summer, the Eiffel Tower quietly grows. On the hottest days, it can stand up to fifteen centimetres taller.
Finished in eighteen eighty-nine, it is eighteen thousand iron parts, held together by two and a half million rivets.
Iron expands as it warms up. Every single metre of it grows about twelve thousandths of a millimetre for each degree of heat.
On its own, that sounds tiny. But spread it across three hundred metres of iron lattice, and one long Paris heatwave adds up very quickly.
The side facing the sun warms and expands first, so on bright afternoons the whole tower leans slightly, quietly, away from the sun.
So the tower breathes with the seasons. And every seven years, teams of painters coat it by hand, to protect two and a half million rivets from rust.
